Monte Albán sits on a mountaintop overlooking Oaxaca. Stone platforms, temple structures and ball courts remain across this extensive site. As you walk through the complex, you can look out over the surrounding valley.

A visit to Monte Albán offers a glimpse of Zapotec life and the layout of their ceremonial center. Tours around Oaxaca often combine the site with visits to artisan villages.

## Monterrey — Mexico's "Sultan of the North"!

Monterrey is Mexico's wealthiest city, sometimes called the "Sultan of the North", and a major trading and commercial center. The city is surrounded by the Sierra Madre mountains. It has the highest level of education in Mexico.

Monterrey is also one of the country's most interesting tourist centers. Visitors will find restaurants, modern shopping malls, numerous museums and cultural attractions. In the nearby mountains, canyons and deserts, they can go mountain biking or explore caves.

## Things to Do in Monterrey!

Monterrey is the hottest city in Mexico, with summer temperatures reaching 40 degrees. The mountains, canyons and deserts surrounding the city offer pleasant escapes and a wide range of outdoor activities, many of which are not easily accessible elsewhere in Mexico. Some of the best natural areas for hiking, mountain biking and cave exploration are very close to the city.

Beyond Monterrico's open ocean shore lies a world of calm water. Channels wind between mangrove trees, their roots standing at the water's edge while the greenery is reflected in the surface. A boat is a convenient way to explore this coastal forest and watch birds.

The mangrove waterways form part of Monterrico's natural area. Local residents offer boat trips along the channels, introducing visitors to the plants and animals of the wetlands. Specific bird sightings depend on nature.

On the eight-day tour, a trip through the mangroves is offered as an option during a free day in Monterrico. This is an additional activity: the route, guiding arrangements, duration and price are agreed before the trip.

At the Monterrico Turtle Conservation Center, visitors can learn how sea turtles are protected along the Pacific coast. Eggs are moved to prepared incubation areas, and once the turtles hatch, the young are released onto the beach, where they make their own way to the water.

The center is run by CECON at the University of San Carlos. A visit offers an insight into the care required to protect turtle nests and the first hours of the hatchlings' lives. During releases, staff explain the rules to visitors and talk about conservation work.

A visit to the center is offered as an optional activity during the tour's stay in Monterrico. Taking part in a release depends on whether turtles have hatched and on the center's current program; it cannot be guaranteed on any given travel day.

In Monterrico, you'll want to kick off your shoes and head down to the ocean. Dark volcanic sand stretches along the shore, palm trees rise above the beach, and waves roll toward the land in long white lines. Travelers come here to unwind after the highland roads, markets and colonial towns.

The settlement lies on Guatemala's Pacific coast in the department of Santa Rosa. Mangrove waterways and a sea turtle conservation center are close to the beach. Both can easily be combined with time by the ocean; available activities depend on the season.

The "Discover Guatemala" tour includes two nights in Monterrico. After the transfer from Antigua, there is a free day to relax on the beach or take optional outings. Accommodation is listed as Dos Mundos Pacífico or a similar hotel.
